Write a complete short story of about 450 words in 5 to 8 paragraphs. Output only the story.

message.content:
The lighthouse keeper, Silas, squinted at the horizon. Another storm was brewing, the kind that clawed at the stone walls of his solitary post and rattled the immense lens. He’d seen countless storms in his fifty years guarding the jagged coast of Aethelgard, but this one felt different. A low hum vibrated through the very foundation of the tower, a resonance that tickled his teeth and made the seabirds scatter with frantic cries. He adjusted his thick wool cap, pulling it tighter against the rising wind. 

His routines were sacred. Every four hours, a meticulous cleaning of the lens. Every evening, a log entry detailing weather conditions, vessel sightings, and any oddities. Tonight, the oddity was the hum. It intensified as the sky darkened, swallowing the last vestiges of daylight. The sea mirrored the bruised purple of the clouds, churning restlessly. Silas checked the lamp, ensuring the fuel was topped off and the mechanism oiled. The beam had to cut through whatever darkness was coming.

He remembered his grandfather, another keeper of this very light, recounting tales of whispers in the storm – tales Silas had dismissed as the ramblings of an old man losing his mind to isolation. Now, the air itself seemed to murmur. Not words, exactly, but a susurrus, a feeling of… attention. He felt watched, not by human eyes, but by something ancient and vast. Something woven into the very fabric of the island. 

The storm hit with the force of a vengeful god. Rain lashed against the glass, blurring the world outside. Waves crashed against the base of the tower, sending tremors through the structure. Silas braced himself, gripping the railing. He’d weathered worse, he told himself, but the feeling of being observed hadn’t lessened. It felt closer now, pressing against the walls, humming within the stone. 

Suddenly, the light flickered. A momentary darkness swallowed the beam, plunging the coast into terrifying blackness. Silas swore, scrambling to adjust the mechanism. He worked with practiced efficiency, his movements born of years of repetition. The light sputtered, then surged back to life, brighter than before. 

As the beam swept across the turbulent waters, Silas saw something he’d never seen before. A shimmering, an iridescence beneath the waves. Not foam, not debris, but a luminous glow that pulsed with the same rhythm as the hum. It receded as quickly as it appeared, vanishing into the depths.

The storm gradually subsided, leaving behind a bruised and battered sky. The hum faded, replaced by the familiar roar of the waves. Silas slumped against the wall, exhausted but strangely exhilarated. He wrote in his log: "Storm of considerable intensity. Light experienced momentary malfunction. Unusual phenomena observed. Further observation required." 

He stared out at the calming sea, a lingering sense of wonder settling over him. The island held secrets, he realized, secrets far older and more profound than any he’d ever imagined. He knew his life, his solitary vigil, would never be quite the same again.
